introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information and Communication Technologies (0796), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two hours. Answer ALL tasks.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group 1, Group 2 and Group 3 (booklets 00/0796/3/G1, G2 and G3): each version has the same three tasks (Task A: Database, 20 marks; Task B: Spreadsheet, 17 marks; Task C: Presentation, 13 marks) with different data, names and cell references.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is require to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

The working files (the workbooks Trift_Loan, Customer_Loan and Worker_Loan, one per group) are supplied on the day in the Candidate folder; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP 1 - TASK B: SPREADSHEET (17 MARKS)**

This task is based on raw data found in a workbook named *Trift_Loan* in your candidate folder. The workbook contains two sheets namely *ACTIVITIES:* and *STATS*. The workbook is designed to manage the finances of a savings and loans meeting that runs for a period of **12 months**. At the end of the 12 months period the interest on loans is calculated using the formula `Simple Interest = Principal amount * Rate * Time` and the savings is paid back to the members together with some interest.

Open the workbook and answer the questions below:

*[Workbook supplied on the day, not reproduced here.]*

questions.enonce_markdown:
Do the following activities in the *ACTIVITIES* sheet,

Enter a formula in cell F2 to calculate the total savings for Mbong. Copy the formula to get the total savings of other members. Write down the formula used in call F5. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: F5: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Layout of the sheet (the printed paper does not show it, it is deduced from the cell references of the questions): column A = number, B = name, C = category (Cat1 or Cat2), D = monthly savings, E = loan taken, F = total savings, G = interest on loan, H = compensation, I = debt owed, J = line total; data in rows 2 to 23, totals in row 24. If the workbook uses other columns, only the letters change.*

The savings are paid monthly for the 12 months of the meeting, so the **total savings = monthly savings x 12**. In the first cell named by the question (F2, the row of Mbong) the formula is `=D2*12`; it is copied to the other rows with the fill handle (double-click the small square at the bottom right of the cell), and the *relative* reference D2 becomes D5 in the cell asked (F5):

```
F5: =D5*12
```

Equivalent form accepted: `=12*D5`. The formula must start with `=`, use a cell reference (not the typed value of the savings), and be filled down for all the members. Illustration with invented data (not from the paper): monthly savings of 20,000 give 20,000 x 12 = **240,000**.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the formula (monthly savings x 12), 1 mark for the copy to the other members (relative references).

questions.enonce_markdown:
When members take loans, their interest per month is calculated depending on the status of the member. Category 1 (Cat1) members pay an interest rate of 1.5% on the loan taken, while Category 2 (Cat2) members pay 2.5%.

Enter a formula in cell G12, to determine the interest on the loan taken by Mbong at the end of the 12 month period. Also compute the interest on loan for all the other members. Write down the formula used in cell G12. *[3 marks]*

*(answer line: G12: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(Sheet layout as deduced in question 1: C = category, D = monthly savings, E = loan taken, F = total savings, G = interest on loan, H = compensation, I = debt owed, J = line total; data in rows 2 to 23.)*

The interest is a **simple interest**: Interest = Principal x Rate x Time. The principal is the loan taken (column E), the rate depends on the category in column C (1.5% a month for Cat1, 2.5% a month for Cat2) and the time is the 12 months of the meeting. The rate is chosen with the `IF` function:

```
G12: =E12*IF(C12="Cat1",1.5%,2.5%)*12
```

The formula is typed once in the first cell named by the question (G12) and copied to the other rows; in the cell asked (G12) the references become C12 and E12. (The question names G12 twice; since the row of Mbong is row 2 in the other questions, the first cell is most likely G2: the formula follows the same pattern.) Equivalent: `=IF(C12="Cat1",E12*0.015*12,E12*0.025*12)`. Illustration with invented data: a loan of 50,000 taken by a member of category Cat1 gives 50,000 x 1.5% x 12 = **9,000**; for a member of category Cat2 it gives 50,000 x 2.5% x 12 = **15,000**.

*Marking:* 1 mark for principal x rate x 12, 1 mark for the choice of the rate with `IF` on the category, 1 mark for correct references and the copy to the other members.

questions.enonce_markdown:
At the end of the session, a compensation of 1% of your total savings is given to you as interest. Enter a formula to calculate the compensation for Mbong in cell H2 and also do similarly for other members.

Write down your formula for cell H10. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: H10: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(Sheet layout as deduced in question 1: C = category, D = monthly savings, E = loan taken, F = total savings, G = interest on loan, H = compensation, I = debt owed, J = line total; data in rows 2 to 23.)*

The compensation is 1% of the total savings (column F):

```
H10: =F10*1%
```

`=F10*0.01` or `=F10/100` give the same value. The formula is filled down the column. Illustration with invented data: total savings of 240,000 give 240,000 x 1% = **2,400**.

*Marking:* 1 mark for 1% of the total savings (reference to column F, not a typed number), 1 mark for the formula valid for the other members (relative reference).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Enter a formula in cell I2, to determine the amount owed by Mbong. Copy the formula to calculate the debt of all the other members. Write down the formula used in cell I6. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: I6: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(Sheet layout as deduced in question 1: C = category, D = monthly savings, E = loan taken, F = total savings, G = interest on loan, H = compensation, I = debt owed, J = line total; data in rows 2 to 23.)*

The debt owed at the end of the session is the loan taken (column E) PLUS the interest on the loan calculated in question 2 (column G):

```
I6: =E6+G6
```

The formula is copied down the column (a sum over the range E:G would be wrong because it would include column F, the total savings). Illustration with invented data: loan 50,000 + interest 9,000 = **59,000**.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the loan + the interest (both references), 1 mark for the copy to the other members.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The line total is the net balance of each member. Enter a formula in cell J2 to determine the line total for Mbong. Also calculate the line total of the other members. Write down the formula used in cell J4. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: J4: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(Sheet layout as deduced in question 1: C = category, D = monthly savings, E = loan taken, F = total savings, G = interest on loan, H = compensation, I = debt owed, J = line total; data in rows 2 to 23.)*

The net balance of a member is what he or she has coming minus what he or she owes: total savings (F) + compensation (H) - debt (I):

```
J4: =F4+H4-I4
```

Illustration with invented data (monthly savings 20,000, loan 50,000, Cat1): 240,000 + 2,400 - 59,000 = **183,400**. The result can be negative for a member whose debt is bigger than his or her savings.

*Marking:* 1 mark for adding the savings and the compensation and subtracting the debt, 1 mark for the copy to the other members.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the totals below each column and bold the row of the totals. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(Sheet layout as deduced in question 1: C = category, D = monthly savings, E = loan taken, F = total savings, G = interest on loan, H = compensation, I = debt owed, J = line total; data in rows 2 to 23.)*

In the row under the last member (row 24) the `SUM` function adds each numeric column. In the first numeric column:

```
D24: =SUM(D2:D23)
```

Then copy the formula to the right up to J24 (the columns E to J get `=SUM(E2:E23)`... `=SUM(J2:J23)`), or select D2:J24 and click *AutoSum* (Home > AutoSum), which writes all the totals at once. The category column C is text and has no total. Finally select the whole row 24 (click its heading) and press **Bold** (Ctrl + B).

*Marking:* 1 mark for the totals of the columns with the bold row of totals.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert cell borders in the range A1:J24 *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the range **A1:J24** (type A1:J24 in the Name Box, or click A1 then Shift + click J24). On the **Home** tab open the *Borders* menu and choose **All Borders** (or Format Cells > Border > *Outline* and *Inside*, then OK). questions.enonce_markdown:
Carry out the next set of activities in sheet *STATS*,

Enter a formula to get the number of Cat2 members in the meeting in cell B2. Write down the formula used. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: B2: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The number of members whose category is Cat2 is a conditional count: `COUNTIF(range, criteria)`. The range is the category column (C) of the sheet ACTIVITIES, rows 2 to 23, and the criterion is the text "Cat2". The formula is typed in the cell B2 of the sheet STATS, so the range is preceded by the sheet name:

```
B2: =COUNTIF(ACTIVITIES!C2:C23,"Cat2")
```

Equivalent forms: `=COUNTIF(ACTIVITIES!$C$2:$C$23,"Cat2")`, `=SUMPRODUCT(--(ACTIVITIES!C2:C23="Cat2"))`. (The layout of the sheet ACTIVITIES is the one deduced in question 1: category in column C, data in rows 2 to 23.)

*Marking:* 1 mark for `COUNTIF` with the category as criterion, 1 mark for the correct range of the other sheet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Enter a formula in cell B3 to determine the highest amount saved by a member at the end of the meeting session. Write down your formula below. *[1 mark]*

*(answer line: B3: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The amount saved by a member at the end of the session is the total savings (column F of ACTIVITIES); the highest one is given by `MAX`:

```
B3: =MAX(ACTIVITIES!F2:F23)
```

*Marking:* 1 mark for `MAX` applied to the total savings of ACTIVITIES.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Enter a formula in cell B4 to get the least amount loaned to a member. Write down your formula below. *[1 mark]*

*(answer line: B4: write the formula in the line provided)*

Save your work and print a copy of your **ACTIVITIES** sheet.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The least loan is given by `MIN` applied to the column of the loans taken (column E of ACTIVITIES):

```
B4: =MIN(ACTIVITIES!E2:E23)
```

`MIN` ignores empty cells. If the members without a loan hold the value 0 instead of an empty cell, the function would return 0; to get the smallest REAL loan use `=MINIFS(ACTIVITIES!E2:E23,ACTIVITIES!E2:E23,">0")` (Excel 2019 and later) or `=SMALL(ACTIVITIES!E2:E23,COUNTIF(ACTIVITIES!E2:E23,0)+1)`. Finally save the workbook (Ctrl + S) and print the sheet ACTIVITIES (File > Print).

*Marking:* 1 mark for `MIN` (or an equivalent) applied to the loans.
